q-149601.name: Question 1
q-149601.problem:
Given the joint probability distribution for two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ below, find $\text{E}[Y].$

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.25$ | $0.3$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.2$ | $0.25$ |
q-149601.worked_solution:
Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals.

| $f(x,y)$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.25$ | $0.3$ | $…$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.2$ | $0.25$ | $…$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.45$ | $0.55$ | $1$ |

Therefore, the probability mass function for  $Y$ is given by the following table:

| $y$ | $1$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.45$ | $0.55$ |

Finally, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}\,{f}_{Y}({y}_{i}) \\  & =1\cdot 0.45+3\cdot 0.55 \\  & =0.45+1.65 \\  & =2.1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-149604.problem:
Given the joint probability distribution for two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ below, find $\text{E}[X+6Y].$

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ |
q-149604.worked_solution:
Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. | $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ | ${f}_{X}$ | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ | $0.15$ | $0.45$ | | $X=4$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.55$ | | ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ | $0.35$ | $0.25$ | $1$ | Therefore, the probability mass functions for $X$ and $Y$ are given by the following tables:
$x$ $2$ $4$
${f}_{X}(x)$ $0.45$ $0.55$

$y$ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$
${f}_{Y}(y)$ $0.25$ $0.15$ $0.35$ $0.25$

Now, we can compute the expected values for $X$ and $Y:$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\,{f}_{X}({x}_{i}) \\ & =2\cdot 0.45+4\cdot 0.55 \\ & =0.9+2.2 \\ & =3.1\end{aligned} $$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}\,{f}_{Y}({y}_{i}) \\ & =0\cdot 0.25+1\cdot 0.15+2\cdot 0.35+3\cdot 0.25 \\ & =0+0.15+0.7+0.75 \\ & =1.6.\end{aligned} $$ Finally, using the properties of expectation, we obtain $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[X+6Y] & =\text{E}[X]+6\,\text{E}[Y] \\ & =3.1+6(1.6) \\ & =3.1+9.6 \\ & =12.7.\end{aligned} $$

q-149615.name: Question 6
q-149615.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x{y}^{2}+2}{6}, & 2\le x\le 4,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expected value of $Y.$
q-149615.worked_solution:
The marginal density function for $Y$ when $0\le y\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{x{y}^{2}+2}{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+2x]}_{x=2}^{x=4} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(8{y}^{2}+8-2{y}^{2}-4) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(6{y}^{2}+4) \\  & ={y}^{2}+\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+\frac{2}{3}, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot ({y}^{2}+\frac{2}{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{3}+\frac{2}{3}y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}+\frac{1}{3}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{7}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-143585.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 3, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{3}{2},$ find $\text{E}[2Y-4X].$
q-143585.worked_solution:
We're given $\text{E}[Y].$ So, we first need to compute $\text{E}[X].$

The marginal density function for $X$ when $0\le x\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =[{x}^{2}y]_{y=0}^{y=3} \\  & =3{x}^{2}-0 \\  & =3{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the  expected value of $X$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =3(\frac{1}{4}-0) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2Y-4X] & =2\,\text{E}[Y]+(-4)\,\text{E}[X] \\  & =2\,(\frac{3}{2})-4(\frac{3}{4}) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

q-143576.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}x+y, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

The marginal density function for $Y$ when $0\le y\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(x+y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+xy]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {1}^{2}+1\cdot y-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+y.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}+y, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot (\frac{1}{2}+y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{y}{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{3})-0 \\  & =\frac{7}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-143478.name: Question 10
q-143478.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\pi }\,\operatorname{sin}⁡y, & \,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{2}, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expected value of $X.$
q-143478.worked_solution:
The marginal density function for $X$ when $0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2}$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{2}{\pi }\,\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }[-\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(0+1) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\pi }, & 0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2}, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the  expected value of $X$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\cdot {f}_{X}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\cdot \frac{2}{\pi }\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{8}-0) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
